_comment: Shape stage 2 must emit for stage 3 to consume. The DFD is a Mermaid flowchart and element types come from node shape: [Name] external entity, (Name) process, [(Name)] data store, subgraph trust boundary, labelled arrow data flow. Mermaid cannot carry source locations per node, so file_hints is a side map keyed by node id — optional, but the biggest single lever on evidence quality.

use_cases.name: Registered customer signs in with email and password
use_cases.description: A customer submits credentials to the login endpoint. The application verifies them against the user store and issues a signed token used by every subsequent authenticated request.
use_cases.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  subgraph TB_NET[Internet -> Application Server]
    CUST[Customer]
  end
  subgraph TB_APP[Application Server]
    LOGIN(Login Handler)
    TOKEN(Token Issuer)
  end
  subgraph TB_DB[Application Server -> Database]
    USERS[(User Table)]
  end
  CUST -->|credentials| LOGIN
  LOGIN -->|lookup by email| USERS
  LOGIN -->|identity claims| TOKEN
  TOKEN -->|signed JWT| CUST

use_cases.name: Customer resets a forgotten password
use_cases.description: A customer requests a reset, receives a token out of band by email, and submits it with a new password to replace the stored credential.
use_cases.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  subgraph TB_NET[Internet -> Application Server]
    CUST[Customer]
  end
  subgraph TB_APP[Application Server]
    REQ(Reset Request Handler)
    DONE(Reset Completion Handler)
  end
  subgraph TB_DATA[Application Server -> Database]
    USERS[(User Table)]
    TOKENS[(Reset Token Store)]
  end
  MAIL[Mail Provider]
  CUST -->|reset request| REQ
  REQ -->|create token| TOKENS
  REQ -->|send reset link| MAIL
  MAIL -->|reset email| CUST
  CUST -->|token and new password| DONE
  DONE -->|verify token| TOKENS
  DONE -->|write password hash| USERS
